svg.text: heights in metres above chart datum · hours before and after LOW WATER at the port
HOURS BEFORE AND AFTER LOW WATER
SPECIAL CURVE, REFERRED TO LOW WATER
In the Solent high water is a stand of hours and its time says little; low water is sharp. So the curve hangs from LOW WATER.
1 · LW at your port = LW Portsmouth + the LW difference below; HW and LW heights = Portsmouth's + the height differences.
2 · Mark the HW height on the top scale and the LW height on the bottom one, and join them with a straight line.
3 · Enter the curve with the hours from LW at your port, across to the line, and down to the scale: that is the height.
4 · Interpolate each difference as on the secondary ports page: the time by the time of LW Portsmouth, the heights by Portsmouth's heights.
WORKED EXAMPLE, IN RED: Lymington, 19 September 2024. LW 16:57 UTC, 0.4 m; HW 3.2 m. At 19:57 UTC, +3.0 h from LW: 1.86 m.
WHAT IT COSTS TO READ, MEASURED: 7.8 cm on average and 11.9 cm at the worst hour, over the 707 low waters of 2024, against the Lymington water.
Curve from the Lymington tide gauge (Copernicus Marine In Situ TAC, analysed by us), normalised with the HW and LW a student gets from the Portsmouth table and these differences.
Springs and neaps split by range: the top and bottom 20 % of the year's tides. LW differences are relative to LW Portsmouth, in minutes as hhmm.
* Ports in red have no series of their own in this training almanac: FES gives their differences but not the shape of their tide, so they use the measured curve of their body of water.
Heights above chart datum. Not for navigation.
